title: Cyrus and the Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of Cyrus Vane, founder of the seaside town of Marrow Bay, is exhumed for a memorial reburial, it is found empty—and concierge Yara Joubert, who once worked the night the founder supposedly died, becomes both suspect and sleuth. Her investigation pulls her into the Vane family's thirty-year-old alibis, a land deal that built the town on stolen ground, and her own buried history as an orphan the Vanes quietly paid to forget. The tide eventually gives up what it took: Cyrus's remains, hidden in the sea wall by his daughter, who killed him to stop him signing away the town to developers—and Yara must choose between exposing the woman who once sheltered her and letting a lie stand.
about_author: Freya Amberdale is the pen name of a former night-shift hotel worker who spent a decade listening at the edge of other people's secrets before turning them into fiction. She writes mysteries set in small coastal towns where everyone's memory is selective and the sea keeps better records than the police.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Yara Joubert, concierge at the Hotel Meridian, watches the exhumation of town founder Cyrus Vane from the crowd—and recognizes the undertaker's face when he goes white: the coffin is empty. POV alternates between Yara and Police Chief Okafor. The emotional beat is dread beneath civic spectacle; Yara realizes she was the last staff member to see the body in 1994, making her a person of interest.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Signatures
chapters.summary: Yara digs into the hotel's old ledgers, reconstructing the week of Cyrus's death: a private doctor, a locked suite, and a burial rushed before the coroner arrived. POV: Yara. She finds her own name on a 1994 payroll—hush money she never understood as an eighteen-year-old porter's kid. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your invisibility was purchased.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Yara interviews Odile Vane, Cyrus's daughter, now the town's matriarch, whose alibi—a dinner party of six witnesses—has never been questioned. Odile is warm, generous, and remembers Yara's mother with unsettling tenderness. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: longing; Odile offers the belonging Yara has always been denied, which makes her a dangerous witness.

chapters.title: What the Doctor Ordered
chapters.summary: The retired private doctor, Halloway, is found dead in his bath hours after Yara leaves him a note requesting a conversation about 1994. Ruled accidental. POV shifts to Chief Okafor, who suspects Yara but can't make the timeline fit. Emotional beat: guilt and fear—the case has started spending lives, and Yara knows her note pulled the trigger.

chapters.title: The Sea Wall Job
chapters.summary: Yara learns that in 1994 the town poured a new section of sea wall the same week Cyrus died—an expensive project with no council record, funded by an anonymous donation. POV: Yara, with flashbacks to her first year at the hotel. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the coffin wasn't robbed, it was emptied before burial, and the sea wall was the second grave.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Tight
chapters.summary: Okafor confronts Yara with the hush-money trail; she trades him the dinner-party guest list in exchange for staying free. Interviewing the surviving guests, she finds their stories identical—word for word—which means rehearsed, not remembered. POV: alternating Yara/Okafor. Emotional beat: rising tension as the conspiracy's shape emerges: not one killer, but a town-sized silence.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: A developer's descendant arrives demanding documents proving Cyrus planned to sell the waterfront, triggering the exhumation in the first place. Yara discovers Odile has spent thirty years quietly buying back every parcel—protecting the town, or protecting the secret? POV: Yara. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the corruption theme sharpens as good deeds and crimes become indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A storm breaches part of the sea wall; among the rubble, workers find human remains wrapped in 1994 hotel linens. Okafor seals the site. Yara, recognizing the monogrammed sheeting, realizes she can identify the linen's provenance—and that whoever hid the body will now be desperate. POV: Okafor, then Yara. Emotional beat: point of no return; the tide is giving up what it took.

chapters.title: The Night Suite
chapters.summary: Climax. Yara reconstructs the true night: Cyrus, dying but lucid, summoned Odile to sign the sale; they argued; she smothered him with a pillow, then bribed the doctor, the undertaker, and the guests. Odile catches Yara in the preserved suite, confesses freely—she did it to save the town, and she saved Yara's mother too. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: confrontation between justice and gratitude, power's corruption laid bare.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Resolution. Yara hands Okafor everything, including her own hush-money receipt; Odile is arrested as the town watches, grieving and furious. At the reburial, Yara places her mother's old hotel pin in the grave—belonging claimed honestly at last. Final image: the tide coming in clean over the repaired wall. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; truth cost her a family and gave her a town.
